title: Key fingerprint troubleshooting scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Brief scratchpad collecting breadcrumbs for the odd 401/429 behavior observed from a subset of API keys when calls come from our EU edge cluster (eu-west-2). Primary suspicion: key fingerprint mismatch or proxy caching of stale key metadata, but log patterns also hint at quota boundary race.

High-level symptom summary:
- Some clients intermittently see 401 Unauthorized while others using the same key succeed. Failures often accompany immediate retries that succeed.
- Separate incidents where the same key receives 429 Too Many Requests for a single short burst (2-3 requests) but quota headers in the response claim ample remaining tokens.
- Failures concentrated in eu-west-2 region; us-east seems unaffected.

Observed timelines & representative traces:
- 2025-02-13 22:07:31 UTC: svc-a (eu-west-2) makes POST /v1/generate -> 401. Response body: { "error": "Unauthorized" } Response headers: Server: redwood-edge, Date: Thu, 13 Feb 2025 22:07:31 GMT, X-Request-Id: rq_3a7f, X-Auth-Fingerprint: fp:ab12cd, Cache-Status: HIT
- Immediate retry (same client, 250ms later) -> 200 OK, X-Request-Id: rq_3a80, X-Auth-Fingerprint: fp:ab12cd, Cache-Status: HIT
- 2025-02-14 05:14:02 UTC: svc-b (eu-west-2) burst of 3 requests in 1s -> first two 429, third 200. Response headers (429): Retry-After: 1, X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 120, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 117, X-Request-Id: rq_4b9c.

Commands & probes I ran (local, from eu-west test runner):
1) Simple curl replicate (uses current key fingerprint recorded in vault as fp:ab12cd):
   curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-REDACTED" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hi"}'
   -> sometimes returns 401, sometimes 200. When 401, headers show Cache-Status: HIT and X-Edge-Proxy-Version: 1.7.2.

2) Bypass edge cache (append cache-bust param):
   curl ... "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?__cachebust=1" ...
   -> still occasionally 401, fewer occurrences. Suggests cache contributing but not sole cause.

3) Key fingerprint dump (admin endpoint, requires mgmt role):
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-admin-REDACTED" https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/keys/sk-test-REDACTED
   -> JSON shows fingerprint: "fp:ab12cd" and last_rotation: 2025-01-29T03:12:00Z.

4) Cross-region test (run same curl from us-east runner): consistently 200.

5) Small python loop to emulate 50 quick retries (to detect race):
   # pseudocode
   for i in range(50):
       r = requests.post(url, headers=hdrs, json=payload)
       print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Rate-Limit-Remaining'), r.headers.get('X-Request-Id'))
   -> pattern: intermittent 401s at low rate (1-2 in 50) and occasional 429 bursts in eu region.

Log snippets from edge (redacted):
- 2025-02-14T05:14:02Z [edge-eu-03] rq=4b9c auth=FAIL reason=key-not-found fingerprint=fp:ab12cd cache=HIT
- 2025-02-14T05:14:02Z [edge-eu-03] rq=4b9d auth=OK fingerprint=fp:ab12cd cache=HIT
- 2025-02-14T05:14:02Z [auth-db] key_lookup duration=12ms key=sk-test-REDACTED state=active last_seen=2025-02-14T05:13:50Z

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Fingerprint race / eventual consistency: When a key is rotated or metadata updated, some edge proxies may have stale fingerprint mapping and reject a request until their cache TTL refreshes. The presence of Cache-Status: HIT and intermittent nature supports this.
2) Distributed key-cache corruption in eu cluster: an edge node's local cache might have a bad entry (null) causing key-not-found until refreshed.
3) Transient auth DB timeouts causing auth fallback to deny -> 401. Logs show key_lookup duration normally ~10ms but there are occasional spikes.
4) 429 anomalies: rate-limiter sees a short burst due to retries and then correctly updates remaining tokens. The Retry-After and X-Rate-Limit headers appear inconsistent when Cache-Status: HIT is set (edge returning stale headers).
5) Client SDK retries too aggressively (some SDK version includes jitter bug leading to immediate retry causing bursts) — low probability given mixed client types.

Evidence for/against: 
- For hypothesis 1: Admin key metadata shows rotation a couple of weeks ago and several edge nodes reported Cache-Status: HIT. Bypass-cache reduces but does not eliminate failures.
- Against hypothesis 3: Auth DB metrics show no sustained outage, only ephemeral latency spikes correlating with maintenance window in eu region 2025-02-14 02:00-02:30 UTC.

Immediate mitigation ideas tried / available:
- Increase auth-cache TTL on control plane to reduce thrash (temporary) -> deployed config on 2025-02-15 03:00 but we still saw a couple of 401s.
- Pin edge routing for affected customers to us-east fallback pool (manual routing) -> eliminated failures for those customers but is heavy-handed.
- Quick rollback of last admin metadata push (if safe) — not comfortable without deeper audit.

Next actionable steps (short list):
- Reproduce with a synthetic harness hitting only edge-eu nodes (target single node) to confirm whether this is per-node or global. (assigned: Aisha)
- Add debug logging for key-cache hits/misses including cache version stamp in responses (short term). (assigned: Miguel)
- Run distributed key-cache scrub job to invalidate stale entries in eu cluster (schedule: maintenance window 2025-02-19 01:00 UTC). (assigned: infra ops)
- Audit admin metadata pushes around 2025-01-29 (who, what, rollback risk). (assigned: Jordan)
- Add short-lived diagnostic header X-Debug-Auth: 1 to reproduce deterministic failure mode, capture full auth lookup path trace. (admin-only).

Notes to self / random pointers:
- Check proxy version differences: eu nodes still running 1.7.2 while us-east on 1.8.0 — upgrade matrix might explain cache behavior.
- Customer impact: roughly 0.2% of requests from a few high-volume keys in EU — low total but noisy for those customers.
- Related ticket: JIRA-INC-5178 has customer complaint and sample request ids.

If I return to this in the morning:
- Try reproducing while toggling Cache-Status via header override (if we can simulate revalidation).
- Get explicit mapping of key-id -> fingerprint -> rotation events from IAM logs.
- If authenticated node proves buggy, drain and restart edge-eu-03.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a short incident summary if we confirm root cause.
